issue:
ToWeekString, ToShortWeekString and Format "D" name the wrong weekday when the week does not start on Monday

With `SetWeekStartsAt(carbon.Sunday)` a Sunday comes out of `ToWeekString` as "Monday" and of `Format("D")` as "Mon", and with a Saturday week start as "Tuesday", while `Format("l")` on the same value still says "Sunday"; with the default Monday week start all four agree. I encountered this with the following code:

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/dromara/carbon/v2"
)

func main() {
	c := carbon.CreateFromDate(2024, 3, 10, "UTC")
	fmt.Println(c.StdTime().Weekday())

	for _, start := range []carbon.Weekday{carbon.Monday, carbon.Sunday, carbon.Saturday} {
		d := c.Copy().SetWeekStartsAt(start)
		fmt.Println(start, "->", d.ToWeekString(), d.ToShortWeekString(), d.Format("D"), d.Format("l"))
	}
}
```

golang version: go1.27.1 darwin/arm64

carbon version: v2.6.17, and master at 9c24fbd (2026-09-19)

time zone: UTC

I expected to get:

```
Sunday
Monday -> Sunday Sun Sun Sunday
Sunday -> Sunday Sun Sun Sunday
Saturday -> Sunday Sun Sun Sunday
```

But I actually get:

```
Sunday
Monday -> Sunday Sun Sun Sunday
Sunday -> Monday Mon Mon Sunday
Saturday -> Tuesday Tue Tue Sunday
```

The date is the same Sunday throughout; only the week start changes, and the name returned by `ToWeekString`, `ToShortWeekString` and `Format("D")` moves with it, one day per day the week start is moved. `Format("l")` and `StdTime().Weekday()` name the day correctly regardless of the week start.

This looks like the mirror image of #200 (a Monday printing as "Sunday" with a Monday week start, back when the default week start was Sunday), which was closed in 2023; on v2.6.17 the names are right only for the default Monday start. If you consider it the same issue, feel free to close this as a duplicate.

BTW, this was found by an automated program that writes property-based tests for various open source projects using [hegel](https://github.com/hegeldev/hegel-go) (but it has been reviewed by hand before reporting). We've also potentially found (but not yet hand validated) 29 other bugs in carbon. You can see the tests at https://github.com/hegeldev/hegel-zoo/tree/main/targets/go/carbon. Let us know if you would like us to file the other bugs found and/or contribute the tests. NB the tests are currently LLM generated and probably not yet suitable for inclusion as is, but we're happy to help get them into a better state if you want them.

issue:
`Format` panics on a format string ending with a backslash

Hello,

I encountered an issue with the following code:

```go
carbon.Parse("2020-08-05 13:14:15").Format("Y-m-d\\")
```

golang version: **1.24.1**

carbon version: **2.6.17**

time zone: **UTC**

I expected to get:

```
2020-08-05
```

A format string ending in a backslash is malformed, but `format2layout` already
tolerates it, so `ParseByFormat` accepts the same string without complaining:

```go
carbon.ParseByFormat("2020-08-05", "Y-m-d\\").ToDateString() // "2020-08-05"
```

But I actually get:

```
panic: runtime error: index out of range [6] with length 6

github.com/dromara/carbon/v2.(*Carbon).Format(...)
	/go/pkg/mod/github.com/dromara/carbon/v2@v2.6.17/outputer.go:809
```

In the `'\\'` case, `Format` reads `format[i+1]` without checking the bound:

```go
case '\\': // raw output, no parse
	buffer.WriteByte(format[i+1])
	i++
	continue
```

`format2layout` had the same bug, and it was fixed in 64dcb40 by adding a bound
check. `outputer.go:809` is the only other `[i+1]` in the package and it was
missed. Applying the same guard there fixes the panic and makes `Format` agree
with `format2layout` on this input:

```go
case '\\': // raw output, no parse
	// Ensure we don't go out of bounds
	if i+1 < len(format) {
		buffer.WriteByte(format[i+1])
		i++
	}
	continue
```

This is worth fixing because `Format` accepts an arbitrary string, so a format
value arriving from user input or from configuration crashes the process.

I'd be happy to send a PR with the fix and a regression test.

Thanks!

IsInternalIP misclassifies IPv6 private/link-local addresses and IPv6-transition-wrapped internal IPv4 destinations as external

Affected Version: commit `747ddde`

### Summary

`IsInternalIP` (`netutil/net.go`) is documented as a general "verify an ip is intranet or not" utility:

```go
func IsInternalIP(IP net.IP) bool {
	if IP.IsLoopback() {
		return true
	}
	if ip4 := IP.To4(); ip4 != nil {
		return ip4[0] == 10 ||
			(ip4[0] == 172 && ip4[1] >= 16 && ip4[1] <= 31) ||
			(ip4[0] == 169 && ip4[1] == 254) ||
			(ip4[0] == 192 && ip4[1] == 168)
	}
	return false
}
```

Only IPv4 loopback (via `IP.IsLoopback()`) and a hand-rolled list of three IPv4 ranges are recognized. Every other case, including any plain IPv6 address (`IP.To4()` returns `nil` for any IPv6 address, not just for transition-mechanism forms), falls through to the final unconditional `return false`. This means:

- No native IPv6 private (`fc00::/7`), link-local (`fe80::/10`), or unspecified range is recognized at all, an ordinary internal-network IPv6 address is classified as external.
- IPv4 CGNAT (`100.64.0.0/10`, RFC 6598) is not recognized.
- IPv6 transition-mechanism forms (NAT64, 6to4, Teredo) that embed an internal IPv4 destination such as `169.254.169.254` (cloud instance metadata on AWS/GCP/Azure) are not recognized, since none of them normalize via `To4()`.

### Details / PoC / Impact

Live-verified by calling the shipped function directly:

```go
IsInternalIP(net.ParseIP("169.254.169.254"))     // true  (plain form, correctly blocked)
IsInternalIP(net.ParseIP("fd12:3456:789a::1"))   // false (IPv6 unique-local - BYPASS)
IsInternalIP(net.ParseIP("fe80::1"))             // false (IPv6 link-local - BYPASS)
IsInternalIP(net.ParseIP("100.64.0.1"))          // false (IPv4 CGNAT - BYPASS)
IsInternalIP(net.ParseIP("64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe"))  // false (NAT64-wrapped 169.254.169.254 - BYPASS)
IsInternalIP(net.ParseIP("2002:7f00:1::1"))      // false (6to4-wrapped 127.0.0.1 - BYPASS)
IsInternalIP(net.ParseIP("2001::80ff:fffe"))     // false (Teredo-wrapped 127.0.0.1 - BYPASS)
```

Any project using `netutil.IsInternalIP` to validate a user-supplied URL's resolved IP before making an outbound request (the standard SSRF-guard use case for a function with this exact name and documentation) is bypassable by returning one of the wrapped/native-IPv6 forms above from DNS instead of the plain IPv4 form of the same destination, reaching cloud instance-metadata services or other internal-network destinations the guard is intended to block.

(POC available upon request)

issue:
range-val-address: misses nested fields of range values

## What happened

`range-val-address` detects taking the address of a direct field of a pre-Go 1.22 range value (for example, `&value.Field`), but misses a nested field such as `&value.Field.Nested`. The visitor only checks whether the selector's immediate receiver is an identifier; for a nested selector it is another selector expression.

With a module declaring Go 1.21, ranging over `[]item` and appending `&value.field.value` to a slice of pointers produces no warning. The addresses refer to fields of the same reused range variable and therefore point to the overwritten value.

Could the rule walk selector receivers back to the range variable so nested fields are reported too?

inefficient-map-lookup: misses named map types

The rule recognizes maps by checking whether `TypeOf(range.X).String()` starts with `map[`. A defined map type has a named type string, so the rule silently skips valid map ranges.

Reproduction: declare `type namedIntMap map[int]string`, range over a `namedIntMap` using only the key, then immediately compare that key in an `if` (or use the documented `!=`/`continue` pattern). The existing fixture harness reproduces the missing expected match.

Expected: determine whether the ranged expression's underlying type is a map, so named map types receive the same analysis as unnamed map types.

package-directory-mismatch: `ignore-directories` matches substrings of the whole absolute path

### Describe the bug

`ignore-directories` is documented as ignoring specific directories. The rule instead builds a bare alternation (`tests|other`) and runs it against the full absolute directory path with `MatchString`. This causes two problems:

1. A directory is skipped if its name only *contains* an ignored name. For example, `tests` also skips `e2e-tests`, and `test` also skips `latest`, `contest` and `calldepth-test`.
2. Parent directories outside the project are matched too. This includes the default `testdata`. A project checked out under `/home/me/testdata-projects/foo` is not linted at all.

### To reproduce

Using [99designs/gqlgen](https://github.com/99designs/gqlgen) pinned to a commit:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/99designs/gqlgen.git
cd gqlgen
git checkout 79dfb99c09cb55ea285ef5098691fd71d785e133

cat > /tmp/revive.toml <<'EOF'
[rule.package-directory-mismatch]
arguments = [{ ignore-directories = ["test"] }]
EOF

revive -config /tmp/revive.toml ./...
```

### Expected behavior

Only directories named exactly `test` are ignored. gqlgen has none, so all 7 mismatches are reported:

issue:
line-length-limit: silently stops on lines longer than 64 KiB

`line-length-limit` uses `bufio.Scanner` without resizing its token buffer, so it silently stops at the first line longer than the scanner's default 64 KiB limit. The rule also does not check `Scanner.Err()`, which makes the truncation invisible.

I reproduced this with a temporary Go file whose first comment line is 70,000 bytes and whose second comment line is 102 bytes, then configured `line-length-limit` with max 80. Both lines should be reported, but revive returns no failures for the file. If the shorter over-limit line is placed first, it is reported normally.

This matters for generated files, embedded certificates/data, long URLs, and other intentionally checked-in content: the very lines most likely to exceed a length policy are the ones that cause scanning to stop. Since the rule already receives the complete file content, a small fix may be to raise the scanner maximum to `len(content)+1` while retaining the normal 64 KiB initial buffer, then check that subsequent lines are still linted.

var-naming: retains omitted options on reuse

`VarNamingRule.Configure` only assigns fields for arguments that are present. Reconfiguring the same instance with fewer or no arguments therefore retains the previous allowlist, blocklist, `skipInitialismNameChecks`, or `upperCaseConst` setting. The rule instructions require every configuration field to reset to its default before applying new arguments.

schema-merging-behavior v3: index out of range in opaqueMember for a one-member allOf whose $ref is flattened

Found while reviewing the v3 aggregate code. Pre-existing on `main` (a157c2a6).

## Problem

Under `schema-merging-behavior: v3`, `mergeSchemasV3` lets a one-member `allOf` through to the merge when the member is the parent's own union variant (`listsComposition`), so that the child is flattened rather than aliased. If that member's own `allOf` includes an opaque schema (one with `x-go-type`), `opaqueMember` reports it by naming "the other member", and reads `allOf[1]` of a one-element slice:

```
panic: runtime error: index out of range [1] with length 1
```

The generator crashes instead of reporting the merge error it reports for the same shape with two members.

## Reproduction

```yaml
openapi: "3.0.3"
info: {title: t, version: "1"}
paths: {}
components:
  schemas:
    Cat:
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
    Pet:
      oneOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Cat'
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/Ext'
        - type: object
          properties:
            x: {type: string}
    Ext:
      x-go-type: ext.Type
      x-go-type-import: {path: example.com/ext}
```

Config: `generate: {models: true}`, `output-options: {skip-prune: true}`, `compatibility: {schema-merging-behavior: v3}`.

Without the `oneOf` back-reference from `Pet` to `Cat`, the same spec reports the opaque-merge error as intended.

## Notes

- The fix is a guard in `opaqueMember`'s second loop: with one member there is no other member to name, and the error should say what is being flattened and why.
- v1 and v2 are unaffected (they don't have this path).

issue:
stdhttp: mixed path parameter and literal suffix generates invalid ServeMux pattern

## Version

- `oapi-codegen`: `v2.8.0`
- Go: `go1.26.5`
- Generator: `std-http-server`

## Minimal reproduction

Configuration:

```yaml
package: api
output: server.gen.go
generate:
  std-http-server: true
```

OpenAPI specification:

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Custom action reproduction
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /resources/{resourceId}:apply:
    post:
      operationId: applyResource
      parameters:
        - name: resourceId
          in: path
          required: true
          schema:
            type: string
      responses:
        "204":
          description: Applied
```

The generated `std-http-server` registration is equivalent to:

```go
m.HandleFunc(
	http.MethodPost+" "+options.BaseURL+"/resources/{resourceId}:apply",
	wrapper.ApplyResource,
)
```

Registering that pattern with `http.ServeMux` panics:

```text
panic: parsing "POST /resources/{resourceId}:apply": at offset 16: bad wildcard segment (must end with '}')
```

This can also be reproduced without generated code:

```go
mux := http.NewServeMux()
mux.HandleFunc(
	"POST /resources/{resourceId}:apply",
	func(http.ResponseWriter, *http.Request) {},
)
```

Although Go 1.22+ supports whole-segment wildcards, a mixed wildcard and literal
segment is not valid. Registering `/resources/{resourceId}` instead accepts the
request, but `PathValue("resourceId")` returns `abc:apply` for
`/resources/abc:apply`; `ServeMux` does not strip the action suffix.

## Expected behavior

For `std-http-server`, either:

1. generate a compatible route that matches the whole segment, validates and
   strips the literal suffix, and passes `abc` as `resourceId`; or
2. reject this path shape during generation with a clear unsupported-route
   error instead of generating code that panics during server startup.

Literal suffixes on templated path segments are useful for custom action routes
such as `{resourceId}:apply`.

## Additional context

The v2.8.0 trailing-slash and handler-registration-order fixes do not cover this
path shape. A local workaround is to register
`/resources/{resourceIdAction}`, dispatch based on the `:apply` suffix, and set
the original `resourceId` path value before invoking the generated wrapper.

The minimal reproduction snippets in this issue may be used under Apache-2.0.

OAS pattern generation without wildcard {$} causes panic in http.ServeMux due to pattern conflicts

When using paths from OAS spec without proper wildcard `{$}` suffix, the generator registers routes that conflict in `http.ServeMux`, causing runtime panic. The generated patterns should use `"{$}"` wildcard to prevent conflicts. This is because Go's `http.ServeMux` interprets trailing `/` as a wildcard match, leading to pattern conflicts when multiple routes can match the same path.

**Current Problem:**

Generated code creates conflicting patterns that cause panic:

```
panic: pattern "GET /api/test/{id}/test2/" (registered at .../api.gen.go:1001) conflicts with pattern "GET /api/test/test3/" (registered at .../api.gen.go:1000):
        GET /api/test/{id}/test2/ and GET /api/test/test3/ both match some paths, like "/api/test/test3/test2/".
        But neither is more specific than the other.
        GET /api/test/{id}/test2/ matches "/api/test/id/test2/", but GET /api/test/{id}/test2/ doesn't.
        GET /api/test/test3/ matches "/api/test/test3/", but GET /api/test/{id}/test2/ doesn't.
goroutine 1 [running]:
net/http.(*ServeMux).register(...)
        /opt/homebrew/Cellar/go/1.24.2/libexec/src/net/http/server.go:2872
net/http.(*ServeMux).HandleFunc(0x10000200fad701?, {0x140010b6240?, 0x1050993e8?}, 0x0?)
```

**OAS spec causing the conflict:**

```
openapi: 3.0.3

info:
  title: test
  description: test
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /api/test/{id}/test2/:
    get:
      operationId: test1
  /api/test/test3/:
    get:
      operationId: test2
```

**Generated code that causes panic:**

```
func HandlerWithOptions(si ServerInterface, options StdHTTPServerOptions) http.Handler {
    m := options.BaseRouter

    if m == nil {
       m = http.NewServeMux()
    }
    if options.ErrorHandlerFunc == nil {
       options.ErrorHandlerFunc = func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, err error) {
          http.Error(w, err.Error(), http.StatusBadRequest)
       }
    }

    wrapper := ServerInterfaceWrapper{
       Handler:            si,
       HandlerMiddlewares: options.Middlewares,
       ErrorHandlerFunc:   options.ErrorHandlerFunc,
    }
    m.HandleFunc("GET "+options.BaseURL+"/api/test/test3/", wrapper.Test2)
    m.HandleFunc("GET "+options.BaseURL+"/api/test/{id}/test2/", wrapper.Test1)

    return m
}
```

**Working solution with {$} wildcard:**

```
func HandlerWithOptions(si ServerInterface, options StdHTTPServerOptions) http.Handler {
    // ... same setup code ...
    
    m.HandleFunc("GET "+options.BaseURL+"/api/test/test3/{$}", wrapper.Test2)
    m.HandleFunc("GET "+options.BaseURL+"/api/test/{id}/test2/", wrapper.Test1)

    return m
}
```

**Proposed Solution:**

Add an option to generate wildcard {$} suffix for exact path matching in spec file or detect and fix pattern conflict while generating code

**Related issue:** https://github.com/oapi-codegen/oapi-codegen/issues/1952

issue:
HTTP push: large receive-pack requests use Content-Length unlike Git, causing HTTP 413

### Bug Description

Large HTTP pushes can fail with go-git in an environment where command-line Git succeeds because the two implementations use different request framing.

### Observed behavior

I encountered this while pushing through an HTTP intermediary:

- Command-line Git successfully pushed the repository.
- go-git failed with HTTP 413.
- Holding the encoded go-git request body constant, the request failed when sent with `Content-Length` and succeeded when sent without it. Both requests used HTTP/2.

This isolates the failure to request framing rather than the encoded Git payload.

### Difference from Git

go-git buffers the receive-pack request body and sends it with a known content length regardless of its size. Git uses fixed-length requests when the complete request fits within its HTTP POST buffer’s usable capacity, and switches to an unknown-length upload for larger requests.

This behavior is implemented in Git’s [`post_rpc()` and `rpc_read_from_out()`](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.54.0/remote-curl.c) and described in the [`http.postBuffer` documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config#Documentation/git-config.txt-httppostBuffer).

### Expected behavior

go-git should match Git’s default receive-pack request framing: preserve fixed-length small requests and use unknown-length framing for larger requests. This produces chunked transfer encoding over HTTP/1.1 and requests without `Content-Length` over HTTP/2.

The current difference causes otherwise successful Git pushes to fail with go-git, contrary to its stated Git-compatibility goal.

ReaderFromDelta silently returns incorrect bytes after a backward copy

### Bug Description

`packfile.ReaderFromDelta` can return incorrect content without an error when a delta copies backward through the base and then copies forward again.

For the base `abcdefghijklmnopqrst`, copying one byte from offsets `10`, `0`, and `13` should produce `kan`. The streaming decoder instead returns `kac`, with no error.

The same input produces `kan` through `packfile.PatchDelta`, go-git's regular pack parser, and reference Git.

### go-git Version

Reproduced on v6 `main` at `d15c624290f14f5eec6f51a660b20b8449ee7d98`.

### Steps to Reproduce

In an empty directory:

```sh
go mod init example.com/delta-repro
go get github.com/go-git/go-git/v6@d15c624290f14f5eec6f51a660b20b8449ee7d98
```

Save this as `main.go`:

```go
package main

import (
	"bytes"
	"fmt"
	"io"

	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing/format/packfile"
)

func main() {
	base := &plumbing.MemoryObject{}
	if _, err := base.Write([]byte("abcdefghijklmnopqrst")); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}

	// Base size 20, target size 3; copy one byte at offsets 10, 0, 13.
	delta := []byte{20, 3, 0x91, 10, 1, 0x90, 1, 0x91, 13, 1}

	r, err := packfile.ReaderFromDelta(base, bytes.NewReader(delta))
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = r.Close() }()

	out, err := io.ReadAll(r)
	fmt.Printf("%q, %v\n", out, err)
}
```

Run `go run .`.

Expected:

```text
"kan", <nil>
```

Actual:

```text
"kac", <nil>
```

### Additional Information

Tested with Go 1.26.3 on macOS/arm64. Independent checks using SHA-1 and SHA-256 packs matched reference Git's expected output.

When processing a backward copy, `ReaderFromDelta` reopens the base reader at position zero but retains the previous `basePos`. A subsequent forward copy therefore calculates its skip from the wrong position. Resetting `basePos` alongside the reader fixes the reproduction.

gitignore: a pattern with a doubled slash (`a//b`, `c//`) matches paths that git does not

A pattern containing a doubled slash matches as if the slash were single: `a//b` ignores `a/b` and `c//` ignores everything under `c`, where `git check-ignore` matches nothing with either pattern:

```go

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v5/plumbing/format/gitignore"
)

func main() {
	for _, c := range [][2]string{{"a//b", "a/b"}, {"a/b", "a/b"}, {"c//", "c/x"}, {"c/", "c/x"}} {
		m := gitignore.NewMatcher([]gitignore.Pattern{gitignore.ParsePattern(c[0], nil)})
		fmt.Printf("%-6q matches %q: %v\n", c[0], c[1], m.Match(strings.Split(c[1], "/"), false))
	}

```

Output:

```
"a//b" matches "a/b": true
"a/b"  matches "a/b": true
"c//"  matches "c/x": true
"c/"   matches "c/x": true
```

git, with the two lines `a//b` and `c//` in a `.gitignore` and the files `a/b` and `c/x`:

```
$ git check-ignore -v --non-matching a/b c/x
::	a/b
::	c/x
```

- Project: [[go-git](https://github.com/go-git/go-git)](https://github.com/go-git/go-git)
- Upstream checkout: https://github.com/go-git/go-git.git
- Tested revision: 8372f313bbadedba17bb789ec702e6931466be68
- git describe: v6.0.0-alpha.5-111-g8372f313
- Commit date: 2026-09-09T11:00:41+02:00
- Commit subject: Merge pull request #2362 from go-git/feat/http-per-origin-credentials
- Go module: github.com/go-git/go-git/v6
- Affected range: not determined; the behavior is confirmed at this exact
  revision.

The issue is in Repository.RepackObjects, specifically the loose-object
cleanup in createNewObjectPack.

Suggested triage: high-impact repository-integrity/data-loss issue. It should
be handled as a security issue when an application runs repacking on
untrusted repositories and an attacker can influence the conditions that make
pack finalization fail. The reproduction below does not demonstrate a
remote-only trigger for the finalization failure.

## Summary

RepackObjects deletes reachable loose objects immediately after the pack
encoder returns, but the PackfileWriter is closed only by a deferred call.
Closing the writer is part of pack finalization and publication. If that close
fails, RepackObjects returns an error after the original loose objects have
already been deleted. When those loose objects were the only durable copies,
the repository is left with a reference to an object that can no longer be
read and no replacement pack.

This is a destructive failure-ordering bug: the operation reports failure, but
the failed operation has already removed the source data it was supposed to
preserve.

## Technical details

At the tested revision, the operation proceeds in this order:

1. createNewObjectPack obtains a pack writer and registers a deferred
   PackfileWriter.Close() call in
   [[repository.go at lines 2160-2164](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/blob/8372f313bbadedba17bb789ec702e6931466be68/repository.go#L2160-L2164)](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/blob/8372f313bbadedba17bb789ec702e6931466be68/repository.go#L2160-L2164).

   [[repository.go lines 2169-2172](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/blob/8372f313bbadedba17bb789ec702e6931466be68/repository.go#L2169-L2172)](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/blob/8372f313bbadedba17bb789ec702e6931466be68/repository.go#L2169-L2172).
3. The function deletes every loose object reached by the object walk at
   [[repository.go lines 2175-2189](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/blob/8372f313bbadedba17bb789ec702e6931466be68/repository.go#L2175-L2189)](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/blob/8372f313bbadedba17bb789ec702e6931466be68/repository.go#L2175-L2189).
4. Only when the function returns does the deferred close run. The helper
   [[CheckClose](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/blob/8372f313bbadedba17bb789ec702e6931466be68/utils/ioutil/common.go#L132-L138)](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/blob/8372f313bbadedba17bb789ec702e6931466be68/utils/ioutil/common.go#L132-L138)

all file descriptors have closed

gitignore: a trailing `**` matches unrelated directories, hiding untracked files from `Worktree.Status`

## Bug Description

A gitignore pattern whose last segment is `**` can match paths that the earlier
segments of the same pattern already ruled out.

The most damaging shape is the common `**/<dir>/**` form. Given a `.gitignore`
containing only:

```
**/node_modules/**
```

go-git reports **every directory in the repository** as ignored — including
directories that contain no `node_modules` component anywhere in their path, and
even when the repository has no `node_modules` directory at all.

Because `Worktree.Status` stops descending into a directory the ignore matcher
excludes, this silently hides every untracked file below the repository root.
`Status()` reports a near-empty result and callers that rely on it to detect
uncommitted work see a clean tree.

A second, narrower case comes from the same code path: a trailing `**` reached
when the candidate path has already been fully consumed keeps the preceding
segment's result instead of computing its own, so `a/**/*/**` matches `a/f.txt`.

Reference git disagrees in both cases. Per `gitignore(5)`, a trailing `/**`
"matches everything inside" the directory it follows — it does not license a
match for paths that never contained the preceding segment.

## go-git Version

`main` @ ffa616afd85ba272fe85d43156b069a8aa762e4c (v6). The affected code
(`globMatch` in `plumbing/format/gitignore/pattern.go`) is also present in v5.

## Steps to Reproduce

Matcher-level minimal working example:

```golang
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"

	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing/format/gitignore"
)

func main() {
	m := gitignore.NewMatcher([]gitignore.Pattern{
		gitignore.ParsePattern("**/node_modules/**", nil),
	})

	for _, tc := range []struct {
		path  string
		isDir bool
	}{
		{"src", true},
		{"src/pkg", true},
		{"src/pkg/app.go", false},
		{"node_modules", true},
		{"node_modules/react/index.js", false},
	} {
		got := m.Match(strings.Split(tc.path, "/"), tc.isDir)
		fmt.Printf("%-28s isDir=%-5v ignored=%v\n", tc.path, tc.isDir, got)
	}
}
```

Actual output:

```
src                          isDir=true  ignored=true    <-- wrong
src/pkg                      isDir=true  ignored=true    <-- wrong
src/pkg/app.go               isDir=false ignored=false
node_modules                 isDir=true  ignored=true
node_modules/react/index.js  isDir=false ignored=true
```

Expected output, matching `git check-ignore` (git 2.47.3) over the same
`.gitignore`:

```
src/                         ignored=false
src/pkg/                     ignored=false
src/pkg/app.go               ignored=false
node_modules/                ignored=true
node_modules/react/index.js  ignored=true
```

### End-to-end effect on `Worktree.Status`

```sh
mkdir repro && cd repro && git init -q
printf '**/node_modules/**\n' > .gitignore
mkdir -p src/pkg && echo 'package pkg' > src/pkg/app.go && echo hi > README.md
git add .gitignore && git commit -qm init
```

Reference `git status --porcelain`:

```
?? README.md
?? src/
```

`Worktree.Status()` on the same repository:

```
?? README.md
```

`src/pkg/app.go` is missing entirely — `src` was reported as an ignored
directory, so the walk never descended into it.

## Additional Information

Root cause is in `globMatch`
(`plumbing/format/gitignore/pattern.go`), which treats its `matched` variable as
a flag that only ever moves to `true`:

- A `**/<segment>` traversal that runs out of path sets `matched = false` and
  falls through. The next loop iteration is the trailing `**`, and its branch is
  evaluated *before* the `if len(path) == 0 { return false }` guard, so it sets
  `matched` back to `true` for any directory candidate.
- The trailing `**` branch only ever raises `matched`, so when its own condition
  is not satisfied it silently inherits whatever the previous segment left
  behind.

issue:
Clone with RecurseSubmodules fails with bare "entry not found" on a stale .gitmodules entry (divergence from git)

### Summary

Cloning with `RecurseSubmodules` (and any `Submodules().Update()`) aborts with a bare `entry not found` when `.gitmodules` declares a submodule whose `path` has no corresponding gitlink (mode `160000`) entry in the index. The git CLI handles the same repository fine, so this is a behaviour divergence, and the unwrapped error makes it very hard for users to diagnose (see downstream impact below).

This is the same defect as #145, which was closed as fixed — but the fix referenced there (#266) addressed relative submodule URLs, a different problem raised later in that thread's comments. The stale-entry failure is still present on `v5.19.1` and on `main`.

### Reproduction (no network, no auth)

A "ghost" entry like this occurs in the wild whenever someone removes a submodule with `git rm` / `git rm --cached` but forgets to delete its `.gitmodules` section — git never complains about it afterwards, so it tends to stay unnoticed for years:

```sh
git init -b main demo && cd demo
printf '[submodule "ghost"]\n\tpath = ghost\n\turl = https://example.com/ghost.git\n' > .gitmodules
git add . && git commit -m "stale .gitmodules entry"
cd .. && git clone --recurse-submodules demo clone-cli   # works fine, entry silently ignored
```

```go
_, err := git.PlainClone("clone-gogit", false, &git.CloneOptions{
	URL:               "<path-or-url-to>/demo",
	RecurseSubmodules: git.DefaultSubmoduleRecursionDepth,
})
// err: entry not found
```

Verified failing identically on v5.11.0, v5.19.1 and current main (da9f7d8). The failure happens before any submodule network access — the ghost URL is never dereferenced — and also reproduces when the repository has valid submodules alongside the stale entry, and with a `path = ./sub` spelling of an existing submodule (any `.gitmodules` path that is not byte-identical to an index entry).

### Analysis

go-git enumerates the sections of `.gitmodules` and requires each declared path to exist in the index: clone → checkout → [`updateSubmodules`](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/blob/da9f7d8a0e98b475600177348d6ece384a370f36/worktree.go#L154-L161) → `Submodule.update`, where the [`idx.Entry(s.c.Path)`](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/blob/da9f7d8a0e98b475600177348d6ece384a370f36/submodule.go#L268-L271) lookup error — `index.ErrEntryNotFound`, the bare `entry not found` — is returned as-is and aborts the whole clone.

git iterates in the opposite direction: it enumerates gitlink entries in the index and looks up their metadata in `.gitmodules` (a `.gitmodules`-only entry is simply not a submodule from its point of view, for `clone --recurse-submodules`, `submodule update --init --recursive` and `submodule status` alike).

Notably [`Submodule.status`](https://github.com/go-git/go-git/blob/da9f7d8a0e98b475600177348d6ece384a370f36/submodule.go#L75-L76) already tolerates `ErrEntryNotFound` for exactly this case — only `update` does not.

### Proposed fix

Two small changes, matching git's behaviour where it matters and keeping the error informative where it doesn't:

1. `Submodules.UpdateContext` (the path used by clone/pull recursion): skip submodules whose path is not present in the index, instead of aborting the whole operation.
2. `Submodule.update`: wrap the lookup error with the submodule name, so the single-submodule path fails with `submodule "ghost": entry not found` instead of a bare `entry not found`.

I have this implemented with tests and can send the PR right away (plus a backport to `releases/v5.x` — this is where the downstream impact currently lives).

### Downstream impact

fluxcd/flux2#4564 — Flux's source-controller surfaces this as `unable to clone '<url>': entry not found` on any `GitRepository` with `spec.recurseSubmodules: true` whose repo carries a stale `.gitmodules` entry, and the message gives users no hint that a submodule (let alone which one) is involved; full

zstd: Reader over a small bytes.Buffer applies the DecodeAll size limit instead of the streaming window limit

`WithDecoderMaxMemory` is documented as "maximum decoded size for non-streaming operations or maximum window size for streaming operations". A `Decoder` used as a Reader follows the streaming contract, except when the source implements `Bytes()`/`Len()` and is shorter than `WithDecodeBuffersBelow` (128 KiB by default): `Decoder.Reset` then decodes it in one go through `DecodeAll`, and `DecodeAll`'s total-output limit applies. So the same Reader flips between two limit semantics depending on input length.

Reproducer: a 1740-byte frame (no content size, 128 KiB window, blocks that expand to ~34 MB) with `WithDecoderMaxMemory(20<<20)`:

| decoder | result |
|---|---|
| `NewReader(bytes.NewReader(b))`, default buffers-below | `ErrDecoderSizeExceeded` after 21,053,760 bytes |
| same with `WithDecodeBuffersBelow(0)` (true streaming) | 33,966,943 bytes, no error |
| `DecodeAll` | `ErrDecoderSizeExceeded` (as documented) |

Found on master (75489f9) by a differential fuzz harness comparing a fully-async Reader against a default one; the stock fuzzers don't see it because both of their configurations share the threshold. Not a memory-safety problem: the in-memory path stops at the cap.

Proposed fix: when the shortcut's `DecodeAll` returns `ErrDecoderSizeExceeded`, fall back to the normal streaming decode of the same reader (its bytes are not consumed by the shortcut), so a Reader always behaves per the streaming contract and memory stays bounded by the window as documented. PR to follow.

issue:
Statistics not set properly if retry fn is already wrapped

For example:
```
@timed()
@retry(stop=stop_after_attempt(3))
def my_call(...):
  ...
```
After the call yields `my_call.statistics = {}` 

In this case the timed wrapper is before the target call, which I assume is receiving the statistics. (If we wanted to put the `timed` second and time each call inside the retry, this should work fine.)

There are of course may ways to work around this (an additional named, intermediate fn, etc.) but maybe there is a different way to code things so that the target of the retry always receives the statistics. (vs. one up the call stack?)

Also, as a possible option I suggest something like:
`@retry(return_statistics_line)` which would return a tuple that would return the retry statistics and the final value, if any - this would not set anything on the fn object itself.
```
@retry(return_statistics_inline=True, return_after_attempt(3))
def my_call(...): ...

stats, result = my_call(...)
```
This also feels nicer from a multi-threading point of view -- even though we have the GIL in standard python, it just feels cleaner to have this more functional approach as opposed to making sure you grabbed the statistics before you called any other I/O-bound operation that could cause the function to be re-entered on another thread/request and clobbering the statistics.

Snowflake to DuckDB: overlapping Base64 alphabets corrupt encode/decode results

The Snowflake-to-DuckDB Base64 translation uses nested `REPLACE` calls for custom alphabets. A later replacement can rewrite a character introduced by an earlier one, changing encoded data or making valid input fail to decode.

Reproduced on main `5c101a25e72157347994156a497b590d02c4296d` with Python 3.13 and DuckDB 2.0.0:

```python
import duckdb
from sqlglot import transpile

source = "SELECT BASE64_DECODE_BINARY('-_8+', '-_+')"
target = transpile(source, read="snowflake", write="duckdb")[0]
print(target)
print(duckdb.sql(target).fetchall())
```

Generated SQL:

```sql
SELECT FROM_BASE64(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE('-_8+', '-', '+'), '_', '/'), '+', '='))
```

Expected binary result: `bytes.fromhex('fbff')`. The standard encoding is `+/8=`; using alphabet `-_+` gives `-_8+`.

Actual: the replacements produce `=/8=`, and DuckDB raises `ConversionException` for invalid Base64. Encoding also has this problem: alphabet `/+=` turns standard `+/8=` into `++8=` instead of `/+8=`.

A simultaneous character mapping avoids the collision:

```sql
SELECT FROM_BASE64(TRANSLATE('-_8+', '-_+', '+/='))
```

This returns the expected bytes in DuckDB. The existing custom-alphabet test uses `U25vd2ZsYWtl`, which contains none of the changed characters, so it does not exercise this behavior.

Snowflake documents the alphabet's positional mapping and requires the same alphabet for encoding and decoding: https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/functions/base64_encode and https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/functions/base64_decode_binary.

A focused candidate patch with regression tests is available at https://github.com/Sarbajit-Sengupta/sqlglot/commit/96b801b. Both dialect test modules pass (175 tests), and a separate Python-standard-library oracle passed 131 DuckDB execution checks covering partial/default/overlapping alphabets, all 256 byte values, UTF-8, empty input and NULLs. Snowflake itself was not executed.

Disclosed: this report, patch and checks were prepared by OpenAI Codex for the account owner. Opening an issue first as requested for new contributors in CONTRIBUTING.md.

issue:
Spark/Databricks: LISTAGG(DISTINCT x, sep) swallows the separator into the DISTINCT expression list

## Bug

Spark/Databricks mis-parse `LISTAGG` with `DISTINCT` + a separator: the separator is swallowed into the `DISTINCT` expression list, and transpiling the result both breaks round-trip stability and adds a bogus third argument:

```python
>>> import sqlglot
>>> out = sqlglot.transpile("SELECT LISTAGG(DISTINCT x, '-') FROM t", read='databricks', write='databricks')[0]
>>> out
"SELECT LISTAGG(DISTINCT x, '-', ',') FROM t"   # separator became an aggregate expression; bogus third arg
```

With `WITHIN GROUP` the round-trip is unstable the same way:

```python
>>> s = "SELECT LISTAGG(DISTINCT x, '-') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x DESC) FROM t"
>>> sqlglot.transpile(s, read='databricks', write='databricks')[0]      # first pass (from a proper AST)
"SELECT LISTAGG(DISTINCT x, '-') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x DESC) FROM t"
>>> sqlglot.transpile(out, read='databricks', write='databricks')[0]    # re-parse of that output
"SELECT LISTAGG(DISTINCT x, '-', ',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY x DESC) FROM t"
```

## Root cause

`sqlglot/parsers/spark.py` maps `"LISTAGG": exp.GroupConcat.from_arg_list` (FUNCTIONS table). The generic function-args path folds everything after `DISTINCT` into the `exp.Distinct` node, so `LISTAGG(DISTINCT x, '-')` parses as `GroupConcat(this=Distinct(expressions=[x, '-']))` with **no** `separator` arg — the separator literal is now a second aggregate expression. The oracle, trino and exasol parsers already route LISTAGG through `_parse_string_agg()`, which parses `DISTINCT`, separator, `ON OVERFLOW` and `WITHIN GROUP` into their proper `GroupConcat` fields.

Tested on `main` @ e2a8b65, Python 3.13.

## Expected

`LISTAGG(DISTINCT x, '-')` should keep `-` as the separator, and `databricks -> databricks` round-trips should be stable.

`DATE_TRUNC` on a `DATE` returns a `DATE` in Snowflake but a `TIMESTAMP` in DuckDB, and the Snowflake to DuckDB transpilation passes the call through unchanged. Checked on `main` (feb0e08) with DuckDB 2.0.0:

issue:
DuckDB generator doesn't quote some DuckDB reserved words (SEMI, ANTI, POSITIONAL, SIMILAR, ...)

**Fully reproducible code snippet**

The DuckDB generator doesn't quote several words that DuckDB reserves, so the SQL it writes fails to parse in DuckDB. Checked on `main` (feb0e08) with DuckDB 2.0.0:

```python
import duckdb, sqlglot

sql = sqlglot.transpile("SELECT semi FROM t", read="snowflake", write="duckdb")[0]
print(sql)  # SELECT SEMI FROM t

con = duckdb.connect()
con.execute('CREATE TABLE t ("SEMI" INT)')
con.execute(sql)  # duckdb.ParserException: Parser Error: syntax error at or near "FROM"
```

Expected `SELECT "SEMI" FROM t`, which DuckDB runs. The same happens for `ANTI`, `POSITIONAL`, `SIMILAR`, `OVERLAPS`, `FREEZE`, `VERBOSE`, `ASOF` and `CONCURRENTLY` as column and table names, all of which Snowflake accepts unquoted. 30.25.0 already added `PIVOT`, `UNPIVOT`, `LAMBDA` and `SUMMARIZE`, which now work.

Comparing `DuckDB.Generator.RESERVED_KEYWORDS` with what DuckDB reports as reserved (`select keyword_name from duckdb_keywords() where keyword_category in ('reserved', 'type_function')`), these are missing: `ANTI, ASOF, AT, AUTHORIZATION, BINARY, BY, COLLATION, COLUMNS, CONCURRENTLY, CROSS, FREEZE, FULL, GENERATED, GLOB, ILIKE, INNER, IS, ISNULL, JOIN, LEFT, LIKE, MAP, NATURAL, NOTNULL, OUTER, OVERLAPS, POSITIONAL, RIGHT, SEMI, SIMILAR, STRUCT, TABLESAMPLE, TRY_CAST, TUPLE, UNPACK, VERBOSE`. Both categories fail as unquoted table and column names in DuckDB 2.0.0; `column_name` words don't.

**Official Documentation**

- DuckDB keywords and the `duckdb_keywords()` function: https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/dialect/keywords_and_identifiers and https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/meta/duckdb_table_functions#duckdb_keywords

issue:
Trigger failure crashes scheduler or reuses another schedule's next fire time

### Things to check first

- [x] Checked the FAQ.
- [x] Searched existing issues and open/closed PRs for this failure.
- [x] Reproduced on the latest v4 prerelease, 4.0.0a6, and master at fc15dd15.

### Version

4.0.0a6 and master (fc15dd15), Python 3.12.10, Windows

### What happened?

A trigger error can stop the entire scheduler instead of exhausting the affected schedule. This reproduces with the built-in `AndTrigger`: it produces its first fire time, then reaches `max_iterations` while calculating the next one.

`_process_schedules()` catches `MaxIterationsReached` and logs that it is removing the schedule, but leaves `next_fire_time` unset. Constructing `ScheduleResult` then raises `UnboundLocalError`. If a healthy schedule was processed first, the failing schedule instead inherits that schedule's next fire time. I reproduced both cases.

I expect the known due run to be queued, the failing schedule to have no further fire time, and unrelated schedules to keep working. I plan to send a focused fix and regression tests for both processing orders, including the jitter path.

### How can we reproduce the bug?

```python
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta

import anyio
from apscheduler import AsyncScheduler, SchedulerRole
from apscheduler.triggers.combining import AndTrigger
from apscheduler.triggers.interval import IntervalTrigger


def job():
    pass


async def main():
    start = datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(seconds=5)
    trigger = AndTrigger(
        [
            IntervalTrigger(minutes=2, start_time=start),
            IntervalTrigger(minutes=3, start_time=start),
        ],
        threshold=0,
        max_iterations=1,
    )
    async with AsyncScheduler(role=SchedulerRole.scheduler) as scheduler:
        await scheduler.add_schedule(job, trigger, id="failing")
        await scheduler.run_until_stopped()


anyio.run(main)
```

issue:
DST transitions cause APScheduler to incorrectly calculate next trigger times

**Description**
DST transitions cause APScheduler to incorrectly calculate next trigger times.

Given:
a cron trigger of month='', day='', day_of_week='0-4', hour='0', minute='0', 
a last trigger time of None
a current time of pd.Timestamp(2021, 3, 12, 0, 0,0,1,0,pytz.timezone('US/Central'))

APScheduler returns '2021-03-16T00:00:00-05:00' for the cron_trigger's get_next_fire_time() call.

*NOTE: there is a DST transition CST -> CDT at 2AM on 14 March.*
```
from apscheduler.triggers.cron import CronTrigger
import pytz
import pandas as pd

cron_trigger = CronTrigger.from_crontab('0 0 * * 0-4', pytz.timezone('US/Central'))
now = pd.Timestamp(2021, 3, 12, 0, 0,0,1,0,pytz.timezone('US/Central'))
print(cron_trigger.get_next_fire_time(None,now).isoformat())
```

**Expected behavior**
To return '2021-03-15T00:00:00-05:00' not '2021-03-16T00:00:00-05:00'

**Additional context**
The APScheduler library determines the next fire time by going through each part of the expression and finding the next viable value iteratively until all parts of the expression are satisfied. When the day is incremented, 24 hours are added. This causes the time to go forward 1 day and 1 hour as DST causes a day to only contain 23 hours.

It seems that the _increment_field_value function needs to be corrected to accommodate DST changes
*NOTE: the same behavior doesn't happen on CDT->CST transitions*

issue:
[BUG] Optional nested schema param returns 422 instead of None when no fields are sent

**Describe the bug**
A schema-typed parameter with a `None` default, such as `f: Optional[F] = Query(None)`, always builds an empty nested dict for `f`, so a request that sends none of its fields is validated as `F()` instead of falling back to the default. The docs advertise `Filters | None = Query(None)` as the supported way to make a schema optional ([docs/docs/guide/query-params.md#L172](https://github.com/vitalik/django-ninja/blob/ea72a759451e4ae3e8b0fd702b489e95f9698107/docs/docs/guide/query-params.md#L172)). If `F` has a required field the request fails with 422, and if all fields are optional the handler receives `F(a=None)` instead of `None`.

Repro (Query only; I did not run Header or Form, which appear to share the same code path, unverified):
```python
from typing import Optional
from ninja import NinjaAPI, Schema, Query
from ninja.testing import TestClient

api = NinjaAPI()

class F(Schema):
    x: int

class G(Schema):
    a: Optional[int] = None

@api.get("/n")
def n(request, f: Optional[F] = Query(None)):
    return {"f": f.dict() if f else None}

@api.get("/g")
def g(request, f: Optional[G] = Query(None)):
    return {"f": f.dict() if f else None}

c = TestClient(api)
print(c.get("/n").status_code, c.get("/n").json())
print(c.get("/g").status_code, c.get("/g").json())
```
Output:
```
422 {'detail': [{'type': 'missing', 'loc': ['query', 'x'], 'msg': 'Field required'}]}
200 {'f': {'a': None}}
```
Expected: `/n` returns 200 with `f` None, `/g` returns `f` None (the declared default).

Cause: `ParamModel._map_data_path` ([ninja/params/models.py#L79-L84](https://github.com/vitalik/django-ninja/blob/ea72a759451e4ae3e8b0fd702b489e95f9698107/ninja/params/models.py#L79-L84)) runs `current.setdefault(key, {})` for every nested path before it checks `if value is not None`, so the intermediate dict exists even when nothing was sent.

Suggested fix (just a suggestion): only create intermediate dicts when the value is not None, i.e. move the `value is None` return above the `setdefault` loop, so the field default applies when nothing was sent. Note this would change the 422 error `loc` for a required schema `Query(...)` with no fields sent, from `['query', 'x']` to `['query', 'f']`, so existing tests may need updating.

**Versions (please complete the following information):**
 - Python version: 3.14
 - Django version: 6.1.1
 - Django-Ninja version: 1.7.1
 - Pydantic version: 2.13.5

issue:
[BUG] Multipart Body str field with quotes or newlines returns 400, and backslash sequences are silently altered

**Describe the bug**
When a view mixes a `str = Body(...)` parameter with `Form`/`File` parameters (multipart), `_MultiPartBodyModel` wraps the raw form value as `f'"{data}"'` and feeds it to `json.loads` without JSON-escaping ([ninja/params/models.py#L183-L191](https://github.com/vitalik/django-ninja/blob/ea72a759451e4ae3e8b0fd702b489e95f9698107/ninja/params/models.py#L183-L191)). The wrap is skipped when the value starts or ends with a quote. As a result, any value with an inner quote, a newline, or a leading or trailing quote misbehaves: a value like `a"b` is wrapped and fails on the inner quote, `say "hi"` ends with a quote so it is not wrapped and fails `json.loads` as-is, `"quoted"` is JSON-decoded so the quotes are lost, and backslash sequences such as `a\nb` (backslash, n) are decoded into a different character.

Repro:
```python
from ninja import NinjaAPI, Body, Form
from ninja.testing import TestClient

api = NinjaAPI()

@api.post("/m")
def m(request, s: str = Body(...), f: str = Form("d")):
    return {"s": s}

c = TestClient(api)
for v in ['say "hi"', '5\'10"', '"quoted"', 'line1\nline2', 'a\\nb']:
    r = c.post("/m", data={"s": v, "f": "a"})
    print(repr(v), r.status_code, r.json())
```
Output observed on the versions below:
```
'say "hi"' 400 {'detail': 'Cannot parse request body (Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0))'}
'5\'10"' 400 {'detail': 'Cannot parse request body (Extra data: line 1 column 2 (char 1))'}
'"quoted"' 200 {'s': 'quoted'}
'line1\nline2' 400 {'detail': 'Cannot parse request body (Invalid control character at: line 1 column 7 (char 6))'}
'a\\nb' 200 {'s': 'a\nb'}
```
Expected: every string is passed through unchanged. Related: #1735 fixed the empty-string IndexError in the same branch but kept the quote-wrapping.

Suggested fix (just a suggestion): for `str` annotations use the raw form value, or `json.dumps(data)`, instead of hand-quoting.

**Versions (please complete the following information):**
 - Python version: 3.14
 - Django version: 6.1.1
 - Django-Ninja version: 1.7.1
 - Pydantic version: 2.13.5

**Prefer `Form`.** Form fields are what HTML forms and most HTTP clients send
by default, and every field shows up as its own input in the interactive docs.
Reach for the JSON body style when the data is nested (lists of objects,
nested schemas) and doesn't flatten into form fields well.

When a `Body` parameter is mixed with `File` or `Form`, how its part is read
depends on its type:

| Parameter type | Multipart part is read as |
|---|---|
| `Schema`, `list`, `dict` | a JSON-encoded string, e.g. `{"first_name": "John"}` |
| `str`, `int`, `date`, `Enum`, … | plain text, e.g. `John` — the same as a `Form` field |

So for scalar values `Body(...)` and `Form(...)` behave the same here; use
`Form` to make the intent clear.

!!! note "Swagger UI / OpenAPI"
    This matches the OpenAPI default encoding for `multipart/form-data`:
    object properties are sent as `application/json`, primitive ones as plain
    text. In Swagger's "Try it out", a JSON body schema appears as a single
    text area — type the object as JSON there — while scalar fields appear as
    ordinary inputs. Generated API clients follow the same rules.

!!! tip
    Path and query parameters can still be declared on the same operation —
    Django Ninja resolves each parameter from its own source regardless of
    how many `File`/`Form`/`Body` parameters are mixed in.

issue:
[BUG] Nullable ForeignKey with depth > 0 is not Optional, so a NULL relation fails response validation

**Describe the bug**
`create_schema(Model, depth=N)` / `ModelSchema` with `Meta.depth` for a `null=True` ForeignKey produces a field whose type is the bare nested schema, with only `default=None`. The default is used only when the attribute is missing. Here the attribute is present with the value `None`, so pydantic validates `None` against the nested schema and fails. The `fields_optional` argument is also ignored on this path (`get_schema_field` returns at `ninja/orm/fields.py:155-156` before `optional` is used).

Relevant code (permalinks at 40e28d4): [`ninja/orm/fields.py:155-156`](https://github.com/vitalik/django-ninja/blob/40e28d4ce0e939c1d015e271547946e61b17c43a/ninja/orm/fields.py#L155-L156) and [`ninja/orm/fields.py:234-252`](https://github.com/vitalik/django-ninja/blob/40e28d4ce0e939c1d015e271547946e61b17c43a/ninja/orm/fields.py#L234-L252) (`get_related_field_schema` sets `default = None` when `field.null` but never wraps the type in `Optional`).

Repro:
```python
class Pub(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=5)
class Book(models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=5)
    pub = models.ForeignKey(Pub, null=True, on_delete=models.CASCADE)

S = create_schema(Book, fields=["id", "pub"], depth=1)
S.model_validate(Book(id=1, pub=None))
```
Output:
```
ValidationError: 1 validation error for Book
pub.name
  Field required [type=missing, input_value=<DjangoGetter: None>, input_type=DjangoGetter]
```
Expected: `pub=None`. A list endpoint containing a book that has no publisher returns a 500.

Suggested fix (a suggestion only): pass `optional` into `get_related_field_schema` and return `Optional[schema]` when the default is `None` (nullable field or optional). For many-to-many, whether to wrap `List[schema]` in `Optional` only when `optional` is set is a design choice for the maintainers.

**Versions (please complete the following information):**
 - Python version: 3.14.0
 - Django version: 6.1.1
 - Django-Ninja version: 1.7.1
 - Pydantic version: 2.13.5

issue:
[BUG] CursorPagination returns 500 when >= NINJA_PAGINATION_MAX_OFFSET rows share the page-boundary ordering value

**Describe the bug**
`Cursor.o` is declared with `lt=settings.PAGINATION_MAX_OFFSET` (default 100): https://github.com/vitalik/django-ninja/blob/40e28d4ce0e939c1d015e271547946e61b17c43a/ninja/pagination.py#L263-L269

The same model is used to build the outgoing next/previous cursors (`self.Cursor(o=offset, ...)`, [L379](https://github.com/vitalik/django-ninja/blob/40e28d4ce0e939c1d015e271547946e61b17c43a/ninja/pagination.py#L379) and [L423](https://github.com/vitalik/django-ninja/blob/40e28d4ce0e939c1d015e271547946e61b17c43a/ninja/pagination.py#L423)). `offset` counts the rows tied on the first ordering value at the page edge (or `current.o + len(results)` while a tie run continues). Because `lt` is exclusive, the failure happens exactly when the tie run reaches 100 rows (`offset == PAGINATION_MAX_OFFSET`): pydantic then rejects the cursor that the server itself just built, and the client gets a 500. With 99 tied rows everything still works.

The docs describe the max offset as a safeguard against malicious client cursors, not as a limit on valid data.

Repro (model `E` with `d = DateField()`, 250 rows with the same `d`):
```python
@api.get("/c", response=List[S])
@paginate(CursorPagination, ordering=("d",), page_size=100)
def c(request):
    return E.objects.all()

client.get("/c")
```
Output:
```
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for Cursor
o
  Input should be less than 100 [type=less_than, input_value=100, input_type=int]
```
The very first page fails. The same happens when a tie run spans several pages, once `current.o + len(results)` reaches 100. Coarse columns (date-only, status, 0/1 flags) are enough to trigger it.

Expected: a 200 response with a next link.

Suggested fix: move the cap out of the `Field` constraint into a check in `from_encoded_param` (so it only applies to client-supplied cursors, rejecting with ninja's `ValidationError`), and build server-side cursors without the `lt` check.

**Versions (please complete the following information):**
 - Python version: 3.13
 - Django version: 6.1.2
 - Django-Ninja version: 1.7.1
 - Pydantic version: 2.14.0

issue:
[BUG] Django's override_settings does not work for Ninja settings

**Describe the bug**
It seems I cannot use Django's `override_settings` for the `NINJA_NUM_PROXIES` setting.

Specifically, the patched setting **does not** work in this case.
```
@override_settings(NINJA_NUM_PROXIES=3)
@override_settings(NUM_PROXIES=3)
def test_throttle_proxied(self):
```

But this **does** work:
```
@patch("ninja.conf.settings.NUM_PROXIES", 3)
def test_throttle_proxied(self):
```

From what I can understand, for some reason Ninja has its own config that is separate but related(?) to the underlying Django config. It seems to break this standard Django settings patching annotation.

**Expected behaviour**

Patching the settings of third-party Django dependencies usually works fine for me, e.g. I use `@override_settings(AXES_ENABLED=False)` in many of my tests. 

I had a look at how axes handles its application settings. It looks different:
```
from django.conf import settings
settings.AXES_ENABLED = getattr(settings, "AXES_ENABLED", True)
```

For this, it seems to just use the default global settings and sets the default only if the user has not set the setting in their own `settings.py` file.

**Versions (please complete the following information):**
 - Python version: 3.12
 - Django version: 5.2.11
 - Django-Ninja version: 1.5.1
 - Pydantic version: 2.11.5

http server binds to all hosts rather than localhost (#2622 again)

### Checklist

- [x] This is a bug report and not [a different kind of issue](https://github.com/streamlink/streamlink/issues/new/choose)
- [x] [I have read the contribution guidelines](https://github.com/streamlink/streamlink/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-to-streamlink)

### Collaboration

- [x] [I will provide feedback should a pull request be opened with a fix for the problem](https://github.com/streamlink/streamlink/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request-feedback)

### Streamlink version

`5.5.0` through the latest (`8.5.0`)

### Description

I'm using `--player-continuous-http` and streamlink invokes the player with a non-localhost address.

It was previously reported at #2622 and then got fixed. As I can see the bug was re-introduced with #5292.

<hr>

#### Review of the logic before #5292

`output_stream_http` calls `create_http_server` without any arguments specified:
https://github.com/streamlink/streamlink/blob/e9f90896aaa1bd4c6c36ef1f4e1937bd2951eeb0/src/streamlink_cli/main.py#L200
`create_http_server` calls `HTTPServer.bind` with arguments passthrough (in our case nothing):
https://github.com/streamlink/streamlink/blob/e9f90896aaa1bd4c6c36ef1f4e1937bd2951eeb0/src/streamlink_cli/main.py#L160
When no arguments are specified in `HTTPServer.bind`, it uses `127.0.0.1` as the default:
https://github.com/streamlink/streamlink/blob/e9f90896aaa1bd4c6c36ef1f4e1937bd2951eeb0/src/streamlink_cli/utils/http_server.py#L50-L52
So it works just fine.

<hr>

#### Review of the current logic

The logic was affected in #5292, but hasn't been modified since, so it's ok to inspect the current code.
Again, `output_stream_http` calls `create_http_server` without any arguments specified:
https://github.com/streamlink/streamlink/blob/202785df60a325dc3273f8a52c862997fc1f191d/src/streamlink_cli/main.py#L233
Now, `create_http_server` calls `HTTPServer` constructor with `host` and `port` specified, which are defaulted to `None` and `0` respectively, and then it calls `HTTPServer.start_server`:
https://github.com/streamlink/streamlink/blob/202785df60a325dc3273f8a52c862997fc1f191d/src/streamlink_cli/main.py#L200-L209
`HTTPServer` constructor copies `host` and `port` values. Since `host` was explicitly specified, the default value `127.0.0.1` is not applied:
https://github.com/streamlink/streamlink/blob/dc9d0bc36d3560f30427937a59c59488a79eb303/src/streamlink_cli/output/http.py#L27-L30
When `HTTPServer.start_server` is called, the socket is bound to the previously copied `host` and `port` values:
https://github.com/streamlink/streamlink/blob/dc9d0bc36d3560f30427937a59c59488a79eb303/src/streamlink_cli/output/http.py#L60
In the end the server is bound to all interfaces which is not the expected behavior.

<hr>

### Description

`parse_xml(ignore_ns=True)` removes only the default namespace, leaving prefixed namespaces intact. As a result, namespaced attributes are represented by lxml using Clark notation (e.g. `{urn:mpeg:cenc:2013}default_KID`), but `MPDNode.attr()` performs only literal attribute lookups, so `ContentProtection.default_KID` is always `None` for standards-compliant CENC manifests.

1. Edit `class ContentProtection`, adding lines:

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

        self.schemeIdUri = self.attr("schemeIdUri")
        self.value = self.attr("value")
        self.default_KID = self.attr("default_KID")

        log.debug(f'self.attr("default_KID"): {self.attr("default_KID")}')
        log.debug(f'self.attrib: {self.attrib}')
```
2. Run `streamlink` command with manifest file with namespaced attributes as input, e.g.:
`streamlink https://refapp.hbbtv.org/videos/spring_h264_v9/cenc/manifest_prcenc.mpd best`

cli: no output cleanup (named pipe / http server) if stream gets closed before data is available

### Checklist

- [X] This is a bug report and not a different kind of issue
- [X] [I have read the contribution guidelines](https://github.com/streamlink/streamlink/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-to-streamlink)
- [X] [I have checked the list of open and recently closed bug reports](https://github.com/streamlink/streamlink/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3A%22bug%22)
- [X] [I have checked the commit log of the master branch](https://github.com/streamlink/streamlink/commits/master)

### Streamlink version

Latest build from the master branch

### Description

`PlayerOutput.close()` with the necessary cleanup steps never gets called when a `KeyboardInterrupt` gets raised, because `output.open()` does only get called once the first stream data is available, and `close()` depends on the output being `open()`ed first. This means that the named pipe or the HTTP server that was already get created/initialized before the output got initialized don't get cleaned up. In case of the named pipe, this means that it stays as a fifo on the user's *nix system, and on Windows its handle doesn't get closed either.

Fixing this probably requires a bit of refactoring work of how the CLI's `PlayerOutput` is implemented. The CLI's main module should not be responsible for creating named pipes or launching an HTTP server as a way to transmit data to the player. That should be done by the `PlayerOutput` on its own before the player process gets launched.

- https://github.com/streamlink/streamlink/blob/28fd94df49777ceeda368b8739eade3c6d561571/src/streamlink_cli/output.py#L27-L35
- https://github.com/streamlink/streamlink/blob/28fd94df49777ceeda368b8739eade3c6d561571/src/streamlink_cli/main.py#L979-L986

Hello,

My goal is to record automatically streams from a Youtube channel, even if there're network issues on Youtuber end or when Youtuber takes a call that pauses the stream.
Streamlink usually stops recording after 6 to 15 seconds in theses cases.

With or without --stream-segmented-queue-deadline=0, Streamlink exits the same way :

issue:
trio.ssl handling for Unicode (IDNA) domains is deeply broken

`trio.ssl` relies on the stdlib `ssl` module for hostname checking. Unfortunately, when it comes to non-ASCII domain names, it's [totally broken](https://github.com/python-trio/trio/issues/11#issuecomment-307027404). Which means that `trio.ssl` is also totally broken. In other ways, trio handles IDNA well (better than the stdlib). But this is hard to work around.

We don't have a lot of great options here. We could:

* Substantially rewrite `trio.ssl` to use PyOpenSSL instead. But this requires adding a bunch of tricky code, and also would break our API. (We currently take a stdlib `ssl.SSLContext` object as input, and it's impossible to read the SNI callback and other critical attributes off of an `ssl.SSLContext` object, which means that it's impossible to correctly convert a stdlib `SSLContext` into a PyOpenSSL equivalent. See [bpo-32359](https://bugs.python.org/issue32359).)

* Hope that upstream `ssl` gets better, or [fix it ourselves](https://bugs.python.org/issue28414#msg295384). Not impossible, but maybe not a thing to hold our breath on either.

* Hope that PEP 543 comes along and saves us.

* ....?

I'm not sure what to do, but at least now we have a bug to track the problem...

issue:
`except*` can break `@trio.as_safe_channel` cleanup

If we `break` out of a loop over some receive-channel created with `@trio.as_safe_channel`, the async generator will be cleaned up in the background, and indeed this works:

```python
import trio

async def main():
    async with inner_generator() as recv_chan:
        async for _ in recv_chan:
            break  # Early exit

@trio.as_safe_channel
async def inner_generator():
    try:
        for x in range(10):
            await trio.lowlevel.checkpoint()
            yield x
    except BaseException:  # breaks if `except*`!
        raise
    await trio.lowlevel.checkpoint()

trio.run(main)
```

..._unless you use `except*`._  

Add one little `*` to the program above, and we instead crash with a `BaseExceptionGroup(..., [GeneratorExit()])` - and if you have an outer generator wrapping around the inner one, you'll instead see our `BaseExceptionGroup: Encountered exception during cleanup of generator object, as well as exception in the contextmanager body - unable to unwrap` error.

Inserting `if eg.subgroup(GeneratorExit): raise GeneratorExit from eg` before the inner `try:` block [here](https://github.com/python-trio/trio/blob/5bfba27b23f9a1f1bac86880b341bcfab54e43f2/src/trio/_channel.py#L553-L555) fixes this issue and I _think_ is the right approach, but I'd love to hear your takes.

issue:
raise_single_exception_from_group causes SystemExit to have no exit status

`raise_single_exception_from_group` was introduced as part of https://github.com/python-trio/trio/pull/3240 and https://github.com/python-trio/trio/pull/3197, but handles `KeyboardInterrupt` and `SystemExit` by wrapping the original exception in an exception of the same type:

```python
# immediately bail out if there's any KI or SystemExit
for e in eg.exceptions:
    if isinstance(e, (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit)):
        raise type(e) from eg
```

Notably, this causes the resulting `SystemExit` to have no exit status, so `system.exit(1)` (or really any other exit status) does not properly set the exit status. I do not see a good reason why the exception should not be raised directly:

```python
# immediately bail out if there's any KI or SystemExit
for e in eg.exceptions:
    if isinstance(e, (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit)):
        raise e from eg
```

Was there a reason for this handling?

issue:
RF03: unqualified Jinja-rendered column references are silently exempted from consistency checking

## Bug

`RF03` (`references.consistent`) silently skips consistency checking for a
Jinja-templated, unqualified column reference, even though the rendered
identifier is a completely ordinary column name a user wrote themselves.

## Repro

```
$ cat jinja_case.sql
{% set my_col = 'customer_id' %}
SELECT {{ my_col }}, orders.total FROM orders

$ sqlfluff lint --dialect ansi --templater jinja --rules RF03 jinja_case.sql
All Finished!

$ cat plain_case.sql
SELECT customer_id, orders.total FROM orders

$ sqlfluff lint --dialect ansi --rules RF03 plain_case.sql
L:   1 | P:   8 | RF03 | Unqualified reference 'customer_id' found in single
                       | table select. [references.consistent]
L:   1 | P:  21 | RF03 | Qualified reference 'orders.total' found in single table
                       | select which is inconsistent with previous references.
                       | [references.consistent]
```

Both files describe the exact same query (`customer_id` unqualified,
`orders.total` qualified, single table). The byte-identical query flags two
`RF03` violations when written plainly, and zero when the same identifier is
rendered through Jinja. Reproduces on current `main`.

## Why this happens

`_check_references()` in `src/sqlfluff/rules/references/RF03.py` skips any
unqualified reference where `ref.is_templated` is `True`:

```python
if this_ref_type == "unqualified" and ref.is_templated:
    continue
```

That guard was added in #7615 to stop the `placeholder` templater's
colon-style bind parameters (e.g. `:colname`, rendered as a bare identifier
that is not a real column) from being wrongly qualified/flagged — the PR
body, review thread and added tests are all scoped explicitly to the
`placeholder` templater. `ref.is_templated` is a generic marker shared by
every templater, though, so the same guard also silently exempts Jinja/dbt
`{{ var }}`-rendered column names — genuine identifiers the user intends to
select — from ever being checked. Nothing in #7615's discussion considers
Jinja; this is scope drift in an unconditional check, not a decision anyone
made about the Jinja/dbt case.

## Expected

The Jinja-rendered case should report the same two violations as the
non-templated equivalent. The `placeholder`-templater exemption #7615 added
should stay scoped to that templater.

I have a fix + regression fixture ready and will open a PR shortly.

The fix should preserve the result by grouping the replacement:

```sql
SELECT (not coalesce(TRUE, false)) IS NULL;

### Observed Behaviour

Given:

```sql
SELECT CASE WHEN TRUE THEN FALSE ELSE TRUE END IS NULL;
```

```sql
SELECT not coalesce(TRUE, false) IS NULL;

import sqlite3

connection = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
for name in ("original.sql", "repro.sql"):

PYTHON

original.sql [(0,)]
repro.sql [(1,)]

ANSI.

SQLFluff 4.4.0, source revision `ad1231eab8ad9951e186f3a695e8e9abc586300d`; Python 3.12.15. SQLite 3.53.1 for the execution checks. No dbt templater.

issue:
Postgres: ALTER FOREIGN TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... OPTIONS crashes with 'Grammar refers to COLUMN which was not found'

### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.

### What Happened

In PostgreSQL, `ALTER FOREIGN TABLE` supports modifying column options using the syntax:
```sql
ALTER FOREIGN TABLE [ IF EXISTS ] [ ONLY ] name [ * ] ALTER [ COLUMN ] column_name OPTIONS ( [ ADD | SET | DROP ] option ['value'] [, ... ] )
```
(See [PostgreSQL ALTER FOREIGN TABLE documentation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-alterforeigntable.html)).

When parsing this valid statement with `sqlfluff parse --dialect postgres`, SQLFluff crashes with a `RuntimeError`:

```text
RuntimeError: Grammar refers to 'COLUMN' which was not found in the postgres dialect.
```

### Expected Behaviour

The statement should parse cleanly as an `alter_foreign_table_statement` containing an `alter_foreign_table_action_segment`.

### Observed Behaviour

```text
RuntimeError: Grammar refers to 'COLUMN' which was not found in the postgres dialect.
```

This happens because in `src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_postgres.py` (line 7532), `AlterForeignTableActionSegment` defines its match grammar using:
```python
Sequence(
    "ALTER",
    Ref("COLUMN", optional=True),
    Ref("ColumnReferenceSegment"),
    optional=True,
),
```
`Ref("COLUMN")` looks for a segment named `'COLUMN'` instead of referring to the keyword segment `Ref.keyword("COLUMN")` (which resolves to `ColumnKeywordSegment`).

### How to reproduce

`test.sql`:
```sql
ALTER FOREIGN TABLE distributors ALTER COLUMN street OPTIONS (ADD opt1 'value', SET opt2 'value2', DROP opt3);

issue:
DB2: CREATE INDEX ... GENERATE KEY USING XMLPATTERN ... IGNORE INVALID VALUES crashes with 'Grammar refers to the INVALID keyword'

### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.

### What Happened

In IBM Db2, creating an index on XML columns supports specifying `IGNORE INVALID VALUES` or `REJECT INVALID VALUES`:
https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/db2/11.5?topic=statements-create-index
`CREATE INDEX ... GENERATE [KEY | KEYS] USING XMLPATTERN ... AS SQL <datatype> [ {IGNORE | REJECT} INVALID VALUES ]`

`XmlTypeClauseGrammar` in `src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_db2.py` defines:
```python
    XmlTypeClauseGrammar=Sequence(
        "AS",
        "SQL",
        Ref("DatatypeSegment"),
        Sequence(
            OneOf("IGNORE", "REJECT"),
            "INVALID",
            "VALUES",
            optional=True,
        ),
    ),
```
However, `"INVALID"` is missing from `UNRESERVED_KEYWORDS` in `src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_db2_keywords.py`. Because the Db2 dialect loads its own keyword set, parsing any XML index with `IGNORE INVALID VALUES` or `REJECT INVALID VALUES` raises:

```text
RuntimeError: Grammar refers to the 'INVALID' keyword which was not found in the db2 dialect.
```

### Expected Behaviour

Statements creating XML indexes with `IGNORE INVALID VALUES` or `REJECT INVALID VALUES` should parse cleanly.

### Observed Behaviour

```text
RuntimeError: Grammar refers to the 'INVALID' keyword which was not found in the db2 dialect.
```

### How to reproduce

```sql
CREATE INDEX idx ON t(col) GENERATE KEY USING XMLPATTERN '/a/b' AS SQL VARCHAR(50) IGNORE INVALID VALUES;
```

Run:
```bash
sqlfluff parse --dialect db2 test.sql
```

issue:
Databricks: ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... ENABLE NOVALIDATE crashes with 'Grammar refers to the NOVALIDATE keyword'

### Search before asking

- [x] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.

### What Happened

In Databricks SQL, table constraints support the `[ENABLE] NOVALIDATE` option:
https://docs.databricks.com/en/sql/language-manual/sql-ref-syntax-ddl-create-table-constraint.html
`[ [NOT] ENFORCED ] [ NOVALIDATE ] [ RELY ]`

`ConstraintOptionGrammar` in `src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_databricks.py` declares:
```python
    ConstraintOptionGrammar=Sequence(
        Sequence("ENABLE", "NOVALIDATE", optional=True),
        Sequence("NOT", "ENFORCED", optional=True),
        ...
    )
```
However, `"NOVALIDATE"` was not registered in `UNRESERVED_KEYWORDS` in `src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_databricks_keywords.py`. Because Databricks defines its own keyword set, parsing a constraint with `ENABLE NOVALIDATE` crashes during parsing:

```text
RuntimeError: Grammar refers to the 'NOVALIDATE' keyword which was not found in the databricks dialect.
```

### Expected Behaviour

Statements with `ENABLE NOVALIDATE` (and `NOVALIDATE`) should parse cleanly under the `databricks` dialect.

### Observed Behaviour

```text
RuntimeError: Grammar refers to the 'NOVALIDATE' keyword which was not found in the databricks dialect.
```

### How to reproduce

```sql
ALTER TABLE t ADD CONSTRAINT pk PRIMARY KEY (id) ENABLE NOVALIDATE;
```

issue:
[0] is being considered a markup tag

Have you checked closed issues? (https://github.com/Textualize/textual/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed) *Yes*

Have you checked against the most recent version of Textual? (https://pypi.org/search/?q=textual) *Yes*

## The bug

* Trying to create a Static with markup=True with predefined text "[0] Hello World".
=> Crash

* Trying to escape the text results in a non-escaped string. 
=> Crash

According to McGugan:
> `[0]` shouldn't be considered a tag and shouldn't need escaping. If it is throwing a markup error, that is a bug. Please file an issue.

Error:
```
MarkupError: Expected markup style value (found '0] Hello World!').
```

MRE:
```python
from textual.app import App
from textual.widgets import Footer, Static
from textual.markup import escape
class TextualApp(App):

    DEFAULT_CSS = """
    /* any needed CSS  here */
    """

    def compose(self):
        yield Static(escape("[0] Hello World!"))
        yield Footer()

    # code that causes a bug here
```

issue:
Changing `Input` value doesn't update cursor position

Changing the `Input` value doesn't update the cursor position, which can result in an 'invalid' cursor position when the new value is shorter.

Here's a quick example to demonstrate:

```python
from textual.app import App, ComposeResult
from textual.geometry import clamp
from textual.widgets import Button, Input, Label


class ExampleApp(App):
    def compose(self) -> ComposeResult:
        yield Label("[b]Enter a number between 1-10:[/]")
        yield Input(
            "999999999999999999999",
            type="integer",
            select_on_focus=False,
        )

        yield Label("[dim]The input value will be clamped after being submitted.[/]")
        yield Label("[dim]Notice that the cursor seems to disappear.[/]")

        yield Button("Check cursor position", variant="warning")

    def on_input_submitted(self, event: Input.Submitted) -> None:
        clamped_value = clamp(int(event.value), 1, 10)
        event.input.value = str(clamped_value)

    def on_button_pressed(self) -> None:
        cursor_position = self.query_one(Input).cursor_position
        severity = "error" if cursor_position > 2 else "information"
        self.notify(
            str(cursor_position),
            title="Cursor position",
            severity=severity,
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app = ExampleApp()
    app.run()
```

issue:
Options added to an empty (or cleared) OptionList after mount are not displayed.

OptionList._update_lines() exits early if the scroll region has zero height, which can be the case when called  from add_options() after mount.

Fix is to refresh the layout before _update_lines().
