issue:
IpynbConverter: lstrip("# ") over-strips notebook title when heading text starts with # or space

`IpynbConverter._convert()` in `packages/markitdown/src/markitdown/converters/_ipynb_converter.py` extracts a notebook's title from the first Markdown heading using `str.lstrip`, which strips a set of characters, not a literal prefix. If the heading text itself starts with a `#` or a space, the title comes out truncated.

Current code (`_convert`, around line 73-77):

```python
# Extract the first # heading as title if not already found
if title is None:
    for line in source_lines:
        if line.startswith("# "):
            title = line.lstrip("# ").strip()
            break
```

`str.lstrip(chars)` removes any leading characters that are members of the `chars` string, repeatedly, until it hits a character not in that set — it does not remove a fixed prefix. Here the argument is `"# "`, i.e. the set `{'#', ' '}`. This works by coincidence for an ordinary heading like `"# My Report\n"` (lstrip stops at `'M'`, which is outside the set), but any heading whose visible title text itself begins with `#` or extra spaces gets over-stripped.

**Repro:**

```python
import io, json
from markitdown import MarkItDown

md = MarkItDown()
nb = {
    "nbformat": 4,
    "nbformat_minor": 5,
    "metadata": {},
    "cells": [
        {
            "cell_type": "markdown",
            "source": ["# #hashtag campaign results\n"],
            "metadata": {},
        }
    ],
}
result = md.convert(io.BytesIO(json.dumps(nb).encode()), url="a.ipynb")
print(repr(result.title))
```

Expected: `'#hashtag campaign results'` (the heading text after the single leading `# ` marker is removed).
Actual: `'hashtag campaign results'` — the leading `#` of the title's own text is silently eaten too, because `lstrip("# ")` keeps consuming `'#'` and `' '` characters past the heading marker.

The same happens for a heading with doubled leading spaces, e.g. `"#  Title"` → `lstrip("# ")` collapses it further than `.strip()` alone would.

**Fix direction:** use a literal prefix removal instead of `lstrip`, e.g. `title = line[2:].strip()` (since the branch already checked `line.startswith("# ")`, so the first two characters are always the marker), or `line.removeprefix("# ").strip()` on Python 3.9+.

Duplicate-checked: searched `repo:microsoft/markitdown is:issue ipynb title`, `lstrip`, `IpynbConverter`, `notebook heading`, `hashtag title`, and `title strip heading`. The closest existing report, #2115, is a different root cause in the same function (string `source` vs list `source` causing character-by-character iteration so the heading is never matched at all) — this issue is about the title text being wrongly truncated once a heading *is* matched.

Percent-encoded Windows drive colon in file URI produces a duplicated drive path

## Description

On Windows, a `file:` URI whose drive-letter colon is percent-encoded (`C%3A`) is converted into a path with a duplicated drive prefix. This causes `MarkItDown.convert_uri()` to fail before conversion.

The equivalent URI with an unescaped colon works correctly.

## Reproduction

```python
from markitdown import MarkItDown
from markitdown._uri_utils import file_uri_to_path

working_uri = file:///C:/Temp/example.md
encoded_uri = file:///C%3A/Temp/example.md

print(file_uri_to_path(working_uri))
print(file_uri_to_path(encoded_uri))

MarkItDown().convert_uri(encoded_uri)
```

With an existing `C:\Temp\example.md`, the output is:

```text
(None, 'C:\\Temp\\example.md')
(None, 'C:\\C:\\Temp\\example.md')
OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument: 'C:\\C:\\Temp\\example.md'
```

## Expected behavior

The percent-encoded and unescaped drive-letter URIs should resolve to the same local path:

```text
C:\Temp\example.md
```

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Python: 3.12.12
- MarkItDown: 0.1.6
- Repository commit: `e144e0a`

## Possible cause

`file_uri_to_path()` calls `url2pathname(parsed.path)` and then `os.path.abspath(...)`. On Windows, `%3A` is not decoded into the drive separator before `abspath` runs, so the current drive is prepended to a path that still contains the encoded drive component.

I searched existing issues for `C%3A`, percent-encoded Windows file URIs, and `file_uri_to_path` with no matching report found.

faults.after: path = os.path.abspath(url2pathname(parsed.path))

[cleanupIDs] symbol is incorrectly removed when its ID is *NOT* used by URL-encoded reference

**Describe the bug**

Last year's PR #1880 fixed the issue with URL encoding of IDs in `href` or `url()`. However, in practical use, we found that due to differences in SVG export tools or improper use, the SVG files delivered by designers to developers often have references to graphics, gradients, etc., in `url()` that are not necessarily URL-encoded.

Here is one of my actual examples (with business desensitization):

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="渐变_1" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
      <stop offset="10%" stop-color="#c71700" />
      <stop offset="60%" stop-color="orange" />
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#5a2100" />
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>
  <rect x="30" y="30" height="150" width="370" fill="url(#渐变_1)" />
</svg>
```

After this SVG was processed by svgo, it became like this:
```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <path fill="url(#渐变_1)" d="M30 30h370v150H30z"/>
</svg>
```

I traced the code and found that during the search for reference IDs, only URL-encoded IDs were used, which led to the unencoded IDs not being matched. As a result, in subsequent processing, they were considered as unreferenced, useless nodes and were deleted.

https://github.com/svg/svgo/blob/8d6385bd9ab49d1d300a10268930238baa5eb269/plugins/cleanupIds.js#L236

I will submit a PR shortly to fix this issue.

issue:
XMP metadata: document info strings are written unescaped (malformed XML)

**pdfkit version:** 0.20.1 (Node build `js/pdfkit.node.mjs`; the browser build has the same code)

## What happens

`MetadataMixin._addInfo()` interpolates `info.Title`, `info.Author`,
`info.Subject`, `info.Keywords`, `info.Creator` and `info.Producer` into the XMP
packet as raw strings. A value containing `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` or `'` (or a
control character XML 1.0 forbids) produces a malformed XMP packet.

The Info dictionary itself is fine. `PDFObject.convert` escapes those strings,
so only the XMP copy is broken. XMP is written whenever `pdfVersion` is not
`1.3`, which includes every PDF/A and PDF/UA document. Validators such as
veraPDF reject the file, and readers that parse XMP may ignore or misread it.

## Minimal reproduction

```js
import PDFDocument from 'pdfkit';

const doc = new PDFDocument({
  pdfVersion: '1.7',
  info: { Title: 'R&D <draft>', Author: 'Q&A' },
});
const chunks = [];
doc.on('data', (c) => chunks.push(c));
doc.on('end', () => {
  const pdf = Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('latin1');
  console.log(pdf.match(/<rdf:li[^>]*>.*<\/rdf:li>/g));
});
doc.end();
```

Output with 0.20.1:

```
[
  '<rdf:li xml:lang="x-default">R&D <draft></rdf:li>',
  '<rdf:li>Q&A</rdf:li>'
]
```

## Expected

```
[
  '<rdf:li xml:lang="x-default">R&D <draft></rdf:li>',
  '<rdf:li>Q&A</rdf:li>'
]
```

## Suggested fix

In `_addInfo`, escape each string before interpolating it: `&` → `&`,
`<` → `<`, `>` → `>`, `"` → `"`, `'` → `'`. Drop the
characters XML 1.0 does not allow (C0 controls other than tab, LF and CR,
U+FFFE and U+FFFF). `CreateDate` is built from a `Date` and needs nothing.

## Workaround meanwhile

Wrap `_addInfo` on the document instance. Swap `doc.info` for a copy with the
strings escaped, call the original, then restore the raw `info`. The Info
dictionary has already been written from the raw values by the time `end()`
calls `_addInfo`.

issue:
Round-polygon shapes do not rescale when a node's width/height change without its position changing

**Environment info**

- Cytoscape.js version : 3.34.0 (latest on npm; same code present on master)
- Browser/Node.js & version : 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/150.0.0.0 Safari/537.36'



**Current (buggy) behaviour**

_What does the bug do?_
getOrCreateCorners in generateRoundPolygon memoises corner geometry on the node's rscratch, but the cache key consists only of the centre coordinates. width and height are used to compute the corners, yet are not part of the key that decides whether to reuse them.

As a result, a round-polygon node that changes size while staying in the same position keeps rendering at its previous size indefinitely. Its bounding box updates to the new size, so edges clip to the new, larger box while the polygon is still painted at the old, smaller one — leaving a visible gap between the node and its incident edges.

Affected shapes
Everything produced by generateRoundPolygon:

round-triangle, round-diamond, round-pentagon, round-hexagon, round-heptagon, round-octagon, round-tag

Not affected: round-rectangle (separate implementation), ellipse, and the non-rounded polygons pentagon / hexagon — all of which rescale correctly.


**Desired behaviour**

_What do you expect Cytoscape.js to do instead?_
Corner geometry should be recomputed when the node's width or height changes, not only when its centre moves.


**Minimum steps to reproduce**
This isolates the caching behaviour and needs no rendering — it can be pasted into the console of any page with a Cytoscape instance:

const sh = cy.renderer().nodeShapes['round-hexagon'];
const rs = {};                                            // stand-in for a node's rscratch

const a = sh.getOrCreateCorners(0, 0, 25, 25, 'auto', rs, 'corners');
const b = sh.getOrCreateCorners(0, 0, 80, 80, 'auto', rs, 'corners');  // same centre, bigger node

console.log(a === b);   // true  — geometry computed at width 25 is reused at width 80
Observed on 3.34.0: a === b is true, and the corner extent is identical (19.41) for both the 25px and the 80px request.

In practice
Render a node with shape: 'round-hexagon' and width/height: 25.
Without moving it, set width/height to 80.
The node's bounding box and edge attachment points grow to 80, but the painted hexagon stays at 25.
Move the node by any amount — it immediately redraws at the correct size, because the centre changed and the cache was invalidated.
Step 4 is what makes this easy to miss: most applications run a layout after resizing nodes, and the resulting position change silently masks the bug. It only surfaces when node size changes in place — e.g. a user-facing "node size" control.

_What do you need to do to reproduce the issue?_

issue:
node.outerWidth() and node.outerHeight() don't take 'border-position' into account

**Current (buggy) behaviour**

_What does the bug do?_

The implementation of `node.outerWidth()` and `node.outerHeight()` does not take the `'border-position'` property into account. It is assumed that the default `'border-position': 'center'` is set.

**Minimum steps to reproduce**

Open the attached html file. Open the browser console and you will see that all three nodes have the same value for outerWidth() and outerHeight() even thought the nodes are visibly different sizes.

[test_outer_width_height.html.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19217582/test_outer_width_height.html.zip)

Also, the texture cache seems to clip the border when 'border-position' is 'outside'. If you zoom in until the cache is deactivated the border is no longer clipped.
